Where did radar see the 2021 floods?

Colour: where Sentinel-1 radar images from 20 and 22 December 2021 show a flood signal. Height: people living there.
Strong signal (both days)18 hexagons, about 47,000 people
Possible signal (one day)195 hexagons, about 941,000 people
No radar signaldoes not mean it stayed dry
Reported floodedplace from news reports
Radar flagged 213 of 4,003 hexagons, where about 988,000 people live (12% of the Klang Valley). Not every flagged hexagon was flooded, and some flooded places are missed.
This is a radar signal, not a full flood map. The images came 2 to 4 days after the peak (18 to 19 December), when much water had drained, and radar misses water between tall buildings and under trees. Treat it as a minimum.
Strong: flagged on both days. Possible: flagged on one day. On two dry days (8 and 9 December) the same method flagged 30 hexagons as possible and 0 as strong, against 213 and 18 on the flood days.
Each hexagon is about 0.74 km². Even in streets known to be flooded, radar flags only part of a hexagon, so the cut-off is low (5.0% of the hexagon).
Orange circles: places reported flooded by news and Wikipedia; positions are approximate (town or area centre).
Kontur underestimates Putrajaya's population (about 8,600 vs about 110,000 in the 2020 census).
Radar: Copernicus Sentinel-1 (ESA), processed in Google Earth Engine. Ground and water layers: JRC Global Surface Water, MERIT Hydro, Copernicus DEM, ESA WorldCover 2021. Population: Kontur 2023-11-01 (CC BY 4.0). Grid: H3. Basemap: © CARTO, © OpenStreetMap contributors.
On phones the map is flat and lighter. Open it on a computer for the 3D view.
